where: Section 2, step 3 (and the qb formula in Section 1)
problem: It says 'y is distance from the centroidal axis'. A distance is never negative, but the formula qb = −(S/Ix)∫t y ds only works when y is a signed coordinate. In the worked example y runs from +50 to −50, so a student reading 'distance' will make every contribution positive and get the wrong qb.
fix: 'Integrate qb = −(S/Ix)∫ t y ds along the path, where y is the signed coordinate of the wall element measured from the centroidal axis, positive in the direction of S (positive upwards when S acts upwards).'

problem: 'top and bottom flange moments cancel' suggests each flange carries a non-zero moment and the two happen to cancel. In fact the net flow along each flange is zero (q runs from +42.86 to −42.86 N/mm), so each flange contributes zero moment about O on its own.
fix: 'The left wall has zero arm about O. Each flange carries zero net force because ∫q ds along it is zero, so its moment about O is also zero. The only contribution is from the right wall.'

where: Worked example, statement of the problem
problem: The load is said to act at the mid-point of the left wall, yet q = qb + q0 is built from the zero-twist condition, so it is the flow for the same shear acting through the shear centre, which turns out 100 mm to the right. The real box loaded at the left wall also carries a torsional flow. Nothing in parts (a)–(c) is wrong, but the step is easy to misread.
fix: Add one sentence: 'The distribution q = qb + q0 is the twist-free flow for this shear force acting through the shear centre. A real load at the left wall is 100 mm from the shear centre, so the actual flow is this one plus a Bredt-Batho torsional flow (5.4).'

problem: 'q values equal and opposite on the two sides' mixes two conventions: the physical flow in the two vertical walls of a symmetric box points the same way (both up), while the signed values round a single loop are equal and opposite. As written a student may think the two walls carry flows in opposite physical directions.
fix: 'A vertical shear through the vertical symmetry axis gives, at mirror-image points, shear flows of equal magnitude. Measured round one loop, the signed values q at the two vertical walls are equal and opposite, because the path runs up one wall and down the other.'
